questions.question: The state machine below defines a deterministic finite automaton $$\mathcal{M} = \langle Q, \Sigma, \delta, q_0, F \rangle$$ over alphabet $$\Sigma = \{a, b\}$$. Which regular language $$L(\mathcal{M})$$ does it recognize?

options.label: C
options.text: $L_2 = \{w \in \Sigma^* \mid w \text{ contains at least one } a \text{ followed by } b\}$

questions.hint: Track the accepting transition into $q_2$ when reading $'b'$ directly after $'a'$.
questions.explanation: State $q_1$ signifies that the most recently seen character was $'a'$. Reading $'b'$ moves into accepting state $q_2$. Any subsequent $'b'$ keeps the machine in accepting state $q_2$, recognizing words ending with substring $ab$.

questions.question: According to the Pumping Lemma for regular languages, for any regular language $$L$$ with pumping length $$p$$, any string $$s \in L$$ with $$|s| \ge p$$ can be divided as $$s = xyz$$ such that for all $$i \ge 0$$, $$xy^i z \in L$$. Which of the following conditions must also hold?
questions.hint: The pumped substring $y$ cannot be empty, and the first repeat occurs within the first $p$ characters.
questions.explanation: The three conditions of the Pumping Lemma are: (1) for all $i \ge 0$, $xy^i z \in L$, (2) $|y| > 0$ (non-empty loop), and (3) $|xy| \le p$ (loop starts within prefix of length $p$).

flashcards.definition: A 5-tuple $(Q, \Sigma, \delta, q_0, F)$ consisting of a finite set of states, an alphabet, a transition function $\delta: Q \times \Sigma \to Q$, an initial state, and accepting states.

finite-automata.definition: A fundamental property stating that every regular language has a characteristic pumping length $p$ allowing string decomposition $s = xyz$.
